interim_finding.finding: The accepted Stage 1 target encodings are fold-isolated but look ahead in time (Step 3A). Their past-only versions are realizable, verified equal to the production encoder fitted on the available rows, and the primary rule encodes all but the cold-start rows. The differences between the accepted and the past-only protocols, and between the random and the chronological splits, are measured on identical rows below. Each is a difference of whole protocols; the Stage 2-3 families are extended by construction, not by experiment

interpretation.contrasts: The past-only protocol differs from the accepted one in several ways at once: it removes same-day and later labels, removes each training row's own label from its encoding, fits edges, rates and fallbacks on fewer rows and leaves the cold-start rows out of its fits. A difference between the two is consistent with a contribution from look-ahead, which Step 3A found in the accepted encodings, but this experiment does not isolate it from the other changes. An interval that includes 0 leaves that difference unresolved; it does not show that the difference is absent
interpretation.lags: The past_updating lag arms keep the lag-0 model, trained on every pre-cutoff outcome, and slow only its prediction-time encodings: what a lag-0 model loses when its incoming features update more slowly. The lag_consistent arms fit the scaler and the model on outcomes known at the cutoff under the lag, with lag-consistent encodings: the cost of operating under that delay throughout

interim_finding.pr43: PR 43 may use the frozen PR 39 training-side OOF evidence as random-split evidence: fold-isolated (Step 3A mechanism b absent) but with every target-derived feature looking ahead in time, and the MLP's early stopping not encoder-isolated. It may not present that evidence, or Stage 4 conclusions built on it, as forward-in-time performance
interim_finding.pr44_45: PRs 44-45 need the versioned candidate contract (distinct feature names, the contact-day time index as a pipeline input, the registered cold start), the isolated early-stopping procedure as an MLP training candidate, past-only Stage 2-3 constructions (not built here), and adoption criteria that include a chronological comparison, not the random split alone
interim_finding.pr49_open: the chronological cascade across Stages 1-4; prevalence-shift effects on calibration, thresholds, abstention and the Stage 2 obligations; past-only NSD and ECI; the outcome-lag sensitivity at cascade level; whether exposed test rows join

pr49_protocol.data: the training split on the PR 42 time index. Whether PR 49 adds the previously exposed test rows is PR 49's decision, disclosed with that exposure

fit_at_each_cutoff.stage1: encoders (past-only rule on the training rows; frozen and updating arms for the predicted rows), scaler, model with the accepted hyperparameters (no retuning in the primary run), sigmoid or isotonic calibrator by nested OOF within the training rows, the F2 threshold from those OOF scores. Under an outcome lag, every one of these is fitted on the training rows whose outcomes are known at the cutoff (known_at_cutoff), as Step 3B's lag-consistent arm does
fit_at_each_cutoff.stage2: NSD, ECI and day x month sources (past-only where PR 45 adopted a candidate, otherwise the accepted fit on the training rows), the bins (the frozen PR 39 cut points, or Commit 4's procedural bins refitted on the training rows), the GLASS rule ILP and the RF router under the frozen operating contract (pr37-stage2-primary 1.0.0)
fit_at_each_cutoff.stage3: EBM and XGBoost, their calibrators (ECE gate) and nested thresholds, on the training rows
fit_at_each_cutoff.stage4: arbiters, weights and the abstention cut (registered coverage floor) on the training rows' OOF table

missed_obligation_report: obligation, window, arm (frozen, updating, recalibrated) and stage
numerator / denominator, observed value, limit and exact signed shortfall (observe_routing), routed rows and positives, window prevalence
status satisfied, violated or undefined: undefined is never compliant, any violation is reported however small, and nothing is refitted or re-thresholded to remove it
whether the same obligation held on the training rows' OOF routing at that cutoff
the claim it bounds: a miss limits the temporal claim for that window and arm; it is a robustness finding, not a pipeline failure, and it is never averaged away across windows
pr49_protocol.pre_registration: windows, rules, lags, metrics, arms and the missed-obligation report are fixed by this design before PR 49 examines any chronological cascade result

prevalence_shift.abstention: realised coverage and accuracy on the covered rows against the registered coverage floor per window; the cut is not moved to meet the floor
prevalence_shift.calibration: calibration in the large (mean predicted vs observed), reliability curve, Brier and ECE per window with the cutoff calibrator; a prior-shift-corrected curve as a labelled diagnostic
prevalence_shift.measure: each window's subscription rate beside its training rows' (about 3-6% in 2008, 34-60% from 2009-06)
prevalence_shift.stage2_obligations: Pass 1 NPV (>= 0.95), the Pass 1 leakage share of all positives (<= 0.15) and Pass 2 precision (>= 0.30) observed per window with shared.stage2.obligations.observe_routing; support floors are fit-time only. With rules frozen, a higher prevalence lowers Pass 1 NPV and raises Pass 2 precision, so the NPV floor and the leakage share are the obligations at risk in the high-prevalence windows
prevalence_shift.thresholds: F2, recall, precision and the confusion counts at the frozen threshold per window, beside the window's own F2-optimal threshold as a diagnostic only

pr49_protocol.prior_shift_attribution: for every window and obligation, the observed value beside its pure-prior-shift projection from the training OOF class-conditional routing rates (stage2_prevalence_projection): the projection says what the prevalence alone predicts, the difference is the change in routing rates (covariate or concept shift). Step 3B's projection for the frozen routing: GLASS meets all three obligations only for prevalence between about 10.9% and 12.0%; the RF router's training OOF leakage share already exceeds the ceiling, and a prior shift does not move it

split.gap: none in the primary run; a one-period gap is the outcome-lag sensitivity
split.windows: the Step 3B windows (registration): 2008-05..2008-08 train only, then consecutive windows of at least 1,500 rows; each window is predicted by a cascade fitted on every earlier row and frozen at the window's first day

pr49_protocol.status: designed in PR 42 Step 3B; executed in PR 49; reported as temporal robustness evidence, never as independent validation
updated_after_cutoff: only the label statistics of past-only encodings, under the registered rule and lag, as outcomes arrive (the updating arm)
nothing else: models, calibrators, thresholds, bins, routes, rules and the abstention cut stay frozen within a window
a separately labelled recalibration arm may refit calibrators and thresholds on labels known before each window; it is reported beside the frozen arm and never replaces it

chronological_encodings.accepted_window: the production encoder fitted on the training rows (all their labels), applied in-sample to them and to the predicted window
chronological_encodings.lag_consistent: operation under the rule's outcome delay throughout: the scaler and the model are fitted on the training rows whose outcome is known at the cutoff (contacted before cutoff - L; before the cutoff for the monthly rule) and that the rule encodes, with the rule's encodings; predicted rows are encoded by the rule's state at their own contact day. At lag 0 it equals past_updating (checked)
chronological_encodings.past_frozen: training rows encoded by the primary rule; predicted rows by the state at the cutoff, which is fitted on every training row (so the predicted encodings equal accepted_window's, checked)
chronological_encodings.past_updating: training rows as past_frozen; predicted rows by the rule's state at their own contact day, so earlier predicted-window labels enter as outcomes arrive; models stay frozen. Run for every rule with the same lag-0 model, trained on every pre-cutoff outcome: for lag 5, lag 20 and monthly it measures a lag-0 model whose incoming encodings update more slowly, not operation under that delay

content.chronological_windows: the first 4 periods (2008-05..2008-08) train only; later periods form consecutive windows of at least 1,500 training rows, a remainder joining the last window. Each window is predicted by models fitted on every earlier training row and frozen at the window's first day
content.cold_start: rows contacted on the first 3 contact days (plus the lag), or in the first period under the monthly rule, have no past-only encoding. They are left out of that rule's model fits and of every comparison that includes the rule; every state used holds at least 500 rows and 10 positives (checked)

contract_criteria.available: the encoding exists for at least 95% of the training rows
contract_criteria.differs: its values differ from the accepted encoding's on at least 1% of the rows
contract_criteria.realizable: no same-day, later or lagged-out label reaches any row's encoding (invariance)
contract_criteria.rule: a realizable rule whose values differ is a new feature definition and needs its own versioned contract with distinct feature names before any artifact carries it. The primary rule, if available, goes to PR 44 as the candidate; the sensitivity rules go to PR 49. Predictive results are recorded beside the decision; adoption is PR 44's (Stage 1) and PR 45's (Stages 2-3)

content.factorial: on the windows' rows: random/accepted (A), random/past-only (B), chrono/accepted (C), chrono/past-only updating (D). Protocol differences: past-only vs accepted B - A (random) and D - C (chrono); chronological vs random C - A (accepted) and D - B (past-only); interaction (D - C) - (B - A). The past-only protocol removes same-day and later labels, removes each training row's own label from its encoding, fits edges, rates and fallbacks on fewer rows and leaves the cold-start rows out of its fits; a contrast is the difference of whole protocols and does not isolate any one of these
known_at_contact: the row's own covariates (euribor3m, emp.var.rate, nr.employed, contact, day_of_week, month), its contact day and its period
the covariates and labels of the context's rows that the rule makes available
never: its own label, the labels of same-day contacts, the labels of later contacts

mlp_early_stopping.accepted: the estimator draws its early-stopping subset from rows whose encodings (and scaler) were fitted with that subset's labels (Step 3A)
mlp_early_stopping.isolated: the estimator's own split of the rows it will receive is drawn first (train_test_split, stratified, val_fraction, seed 42); the encoders and the scaler are fitted without the subset; every isolated fit checks that the estimator's recorded best validation ROC-AUC equals the ROC-AUC on the reproduced subset

models.lr: accepted GLASS LR: LogisticRegression(saga, max_iter 5000, class_weight balanced, seed 42) with the PR 39 Commit 2 best parameters, on a StandardScaler of its fit rows; P(y = 1), as the accepted tuning and OOF scores
models.mlp: accepted black-box MLP: Stage1MLPClassifier with the PR 39 Commit 2 best parameters and fixed kwargs (200 epochs, patience 15, val_fraction 0.15, seed 42), on a StandardScaler of its fit rows; P(y = 1). Primary rule only

content.outcome_timing: unknown. Each row is a client's last contact of the campaign and its label the campaign outcome; when that outcome became known is not recorded. Lag 0 assumes it is known by the next contact day; lags 5 and 20 contact days (about a week and a month) and the monthly rule are the sensitivities
content.paired_comparison: DeLong (midranks) on identical rows, 95% normal interval; pooled over the rows and per segment (burn-in, W1..Wn); the factorial also reports the unweighted mean over windows with independent-window standard errors
content.question: Do past-only Stage 1 target encodings, which use only labels known when a row is scored, change predictive performance, and how much of any difference comes from the encoding rather than from the evaluation split?

revisions.unchanged: every 1.0.0 comparison's protocols, rows and computation

rules.accepted: the production LRFeatureEngineer fitted once on all of a fit's rows (a random fold, a chronological training window, the full split): the edges, bin rates, median fallback, cell rates and global prior use the labels of earlier, same-day and later contacts (Step 3A mechanisms a and c)
rules.past_daily_lagL: refitted before each contact day d on the context's rows contacted on days < d - L: the qcut edges (from those rows' euribor3m), the bin rates, the median fallback, the day x month cell rates and the global prior all come from those rows and nothing from day d - L or later; L = 0 (primary), 5 and 20
rules.past_monthly: refitted at the first contact day of each period on the context's rows of earlier periods; every row of the period uses that fit

content.same_day: never used: contacts on one day are simultaneous for this purpose (the data record no time of day, so the order within a day is not known)
content.time_unit: contact day of the Step 3A time index (485 days, 26 periods, training rows)

unseen.cell: a day x month cell absent from the available rows: the available global rate
unseen.euribor: a value outside the available rows' bins, or in an empty bin: the median of the available bin rates (the production fallback)
unseen.pooled_years: cells pool years (as in production): a cell's rate can be a year old when the month recurs
